“It’s the economy stupid” has for decades been the mantra of American political strategists when arguing what voters care about most. In 2026, it’s no different. Polling shows that the cost of living, taxation and the impact of the war with Iran are uppermost in voters’ minds as they head to the polls.

“The cost of gas [fuel] is a cliché for a reason,” says Peter Finn, lecturer in international relations at the University of Greenwich and member of the American Politics Group of UK academics.
